approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a score-ranked population of accepted molecular graphs. It keeps the best 64 records, usually breeds from the upper half through weighted score bands, and builds fresh candidates with graph mutation and crossover. Canonical identity checks prevent repeated evaluations, and a source-relative sulfur rule rejects newly introduced outside-envelope sulfur environments. A Gaussian process learns from every accepted score using integer molecular fingerprint counts; correlated Thompson draws choose which candidates from each fresh pool are evaluated. New accepted offspring can immediately enter breeding, while the complete accepted archive continues to train the predictor.
approach.novelty: Replace the breeding-population policy with persistent physicochemical niche champions: retain the best scored molecule in each fixed mass/logP cell and sample occupied champions uniformly for both parent roles. Local quality competition and direct breeder access form one coupled mechanism. Earlier core-based retention left protected records below the sampling bands; uniform sampling of ordinary greedy survivors weakened source quality; determinant-based batch diversification reduced predicted quality. This test instead preserves locally best alternatives and gives them a real path into breeding while retaining the original GP allocator. It tests whether those alternatives produce useful absolute gains, not whether a map merely fills.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior in code Parent n-1744a1494180 is weak productive exploration from a globally score-ranked breeder population: accepted alternatives outside its preferred score bands have no direct breeding support. All three actual Parent summary.json/run.log pairs complete successfully, with macros 0.643098123844866, 0.563172834083287 and 0.583088384937917, mean 0.596453114288690 and population SD 0.033970329983999. The complete Parent evidence has 648 strict best-parent wins among 4350 accepted offspring, summed positive margins 17.25153528627184 and sequential incumbent gain 5.819415048695712. These do not establish that more diversity would help. Historical n-28dc36ed5be7 directly protected 602 records under Murcko-core retention but none subsequently bred under the unchanged quantile law; its earlier binary-Parent matched delta was -0.029689809698780656. In n-a56491c332aa, uniform live breeding exposed 53199 previously unsupported draws and increased parent wins against weaker sources, but lost -0.04599801243765703 under the ungated count Parent. Current sibling n-9b90d71cc6e1 lowered same-pool similarity 0.6660 to 0.5798 while lowering mean enrichment 0.9888 to 0.7287 and endpoints by -0.038159276809506. Broader SELFIES reachability and a MoLFormer mean blend also lost -0.127509460790014 and -0.068110861671429. Conversely, current full-selector removal lost -0.128182900319982, count-location removal -0.088227186324154 and count-residual-covariance removal -0.037159679513884, supporting retention of the original allocator at these separate conditional boundaries. The concrete untested connection is persistent local score competition coupled to actual breeder access; its efficacy is uncertain, and the contrary examples remain part of this test.

method_change.previous_method: global greedy64 survivors and score-quantile parent draws
method_change.proposed_method: fixed MAP-Elites-style niche champions with direct uniform niche breeding and the unchanged count-GP selector
method_change.rationale: On actual code Parent n-1744a1494180, global survival and quantile draws jointly prevent low-ranked alternatives from reliably receiving breeder access. The inspected earlier core-round attempt delivered zero directly protected parents to breeding, while uniform greedy survivors and current DPP acquisition lost useful endpoint quality. Persistent within-cell accepted-score competition coupled to direct champion reuse tests a distinct connection without removing the useful original count-GP allocator. It is one joint breeder-policy replacement and does not attribute its constituents separately.

hypothesis: Replace global greedy64 survival and score-quantile breeding with one persistent fixed 8-by-8 MolWt/MolLogP champion policy: keep the best actually accepted score per cell with earliest-serial ties, draw each first parent uniformly over occupied champions and each partner uniformly after distinct-identity exclusion, and retain the complete original count-GP Thompson allocator.

finding_summary.headline: Niche champions reached real descendants, but weaker absolute progress lowered the endpoint mean by 0.05519
finding_summary.insights:
This closes the earlier access gap: protected alternatives really did breed, enter evaluation and participate in later leaders. That access was insufficient for useful diversification. Productive typed cores increased from 303 to 386, yet only 485 parent-beating molecules bred later, versus 636 for the Parent; many local improvements were measured against weaker sources. Local niche competition also compressed the ten initial records to eight breeders in every session and retained at most 41 occupied cells, despite allowing 64.

The literature-derived elite-retention and direct-parent principles operated as adapted here; this was not a reproduction of a published molecular illumination system. Descriptor cells did not secure useful molecular context or credible geometry: the chemistry audit found 396 tiny fragments versus 105, more empty scaffolds, and inherited unusual heteroatom/ring environments. Those associations do not identify the cause of the score loss. The experiment supports a negative conditional effect of the joint fixed breeder policy, without separating retention from sampling or assigning chemical mediation. Its registered stopping condition is met, so this recipe ends. Lower dispersion, broader generic frameworks and ancestry participation do not justify a grid or sampler rescue.
finding_summary.results:
The retention-to-breeding connection worked. All 4,500 accepted-record map updates matched the fixed cell, score and tie rules. Across the fifteen sessions, 691 champion records received breeding draws unavailable under the old support; 527 of these were outside greedy retention. Newly supported draws produced 1,795 accepted offspring, including 1,174 from directly protected champions. Every newly supported champion with an actual draw opportunity was used, although 106 produced no selected descendant while newly supported.

Local wins increased from 648 to 738, but their summed positive score margin fell from 17.2515 to 16.9695, and mean offspring score fell from 0.3720 to 0.2898. Sequential incumbent gain fell from 5.8194 to 4.9916, with 214 advances versus 255. The complete endpoint mean was 0.541266 versus 0.596453: a paired change of −0.055187 against the required +0.002. All three seed averages and all five task means fell; twelve endpoints lost and three gained. All sessions completed, with no numerical fallback or missing endpoint.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families coexist with tiny fragments, N-halogen substitution and seed-specific difficult ring geometry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-37a4fc183d94 produces fused aromatic carbonyl compounds, linked nitrogen-rich diones, aryl/aliphatic amines, quinoline-associated nitrogen/carbonyl ring systems, and fluorinated heterocycles. The output has abundant rings and aromatic regions, rather than a general inability to make either. Leaders are chemically different across seeds, but some leading series remain narrow. All 15 Child and 15 published code-Parent n-1744a1494180 search trajectory paths were present and read. Each node has 4500 recorded observations: 4350 optimizer-source observations and 150 supplied initial observations, with 900 total and 870 optimizer observations per objective. The issued seeds are 0, 1 and 2. context.comparison separately reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, with no profile-mismatched seeds; no path, task or matched seed comparison is missing. Initial evaluation/SMILES/score records match within every Child/Parent task-seed pair. Full trajectories supply seed-specific leaders and final proposals; the digest final_molecules excerpt contains seed 2 only and is not treated as every seed endpoint. Only recorded scored observations are characterized here; unscored pools and rejected proposals are outside this molecular inventory. Digest ring-closure incidence ranges from 0.8322 to 0.9552, aromatic-text incidence from 0.7839 to 0.9356, and halogen-text incidence from 0.3402 to 0.9011. These are incidences of SMILES text features among optimizer observations, not ring counts, aromatic-atom fractions or measured chemical properties. All digest stereocentre-string incidences are zero. Independently, read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 parsing succeeds for all 4350 Child and 4350 Parent optimizer records. The Child heavy-atom median is 28, the range is 1 to 114, the perceived-ring median is 4 and the aromatic-ring median is 2; the Parent medians are also 28, 4 and 2. Child observations with at most five heavy atoms number 396 versus Parent 105, and empty Murcko scaffolds number 440 versus 111. Distinct typed Murcko cores are 1717 versus 1740 and distinct generic frameworks 1161 versus 1016, including the empty scaffold as one distinct value in each set. These are graph-identity summaries of optimizer observations, not useful-scaffold or feasibility measurements; they neither establish collapse nor establish productive diversity. Counts across task-seed observations are not counts of independent compounds or independent experiments. Direct graph-bond incidences in Child versus Parent are N-halogen 1033 versus 786, O-halogen 170 versus 217, S-halogen 76 versus 93, and O-O 166 versus 128. A carbon centre bearing two double bonds and belonging to a perceived ring of size at most seven occurs in 129 Child observations versus 6 Parent observations; 127 Child cases belong to the fluorinated seed-0 series described below. This carbon-specific definition excludes sulfur oxides and is separate from the digest text counter. Ring basis membership does not calculate conformations or strain energies. RDKit finds unspecified tetrahedral centres in 2034 Child observations versus 2455 Parent observations, while neither output contains specified chiral atom tags. Child formal-charge-bearing graphs number 27, all in the first objective, versus zero Parent; neutral notation elsewhere is not a measurement of protonation or amine basicity. Questionable synthetic plausibility and weak drug-likeness are qualitative readings of unusual local bonds, unresolved stereochemical identity, small-ring unsaturation and extreme size tails. No synthetic route, stability, toxicity, pKa, solution state, accessible conformation or experimental pharmacology was measured. Recognizable amides, phenols, ethers and cyclic amines remain present, so these judgements are not blanket statements that every molecule is infeasible. Measurements, definitions, per-seed exemplars and SHA-256 hashes of the immutable request and all read trajectories are saved in .slots/L01-resume-20261004/r33-slot0-molecular/measurements.json; the accompanying annotated_trajectories.json retains every read record. The published Parent molecular assessment was read through context.evidence_index.node_path_template. Recurring gaps retain its stated provenance from n-c55c3d520a2c through n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180; only the present paired search panel supports the new counts. Complete quoted SMILES are drawn from trusted Child trajectories or the supplied digest. Score-gradient readings are associations among observed molecules and supplied scores. They do not identify a hidden target pharmacophore, attribute chemistry to retention versus sampling, determine mechanism activation, or assign values to unseen alternatives.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer observations have median 25 heavy atoms versus Parent 24; the Child seed leaders have 24, 25 and 25. Seed 0 yields a fused nitrogen-containing aromatic system joined through a ketone/methylene segment to a halophenyl ring, with methoxy and ethyl groups. Its leader has four perceived aromatic rings and no N-halogen bond. Seed 1 instead yields an aryl amide with an N-N substituent, N-bromination and an aminomethyl N-F group attached to a benzene/four-membered unsaturated fused system; only two of its three perceived rings are aromatic. Seed 2 gives a methoxy/dimethyl indole-like anilide with ring N-F and an N-amino amide substituent, with three aromatic rings. These are distinct molecular arrangements, not one common seed leader. The 20 highest observed labels in each of seeds 1 and 2 share one typed Murcko core within that seed, despite substituent variation. Conventional carbonyl/aromatic motifs coexist with N-halogen and ring-topology concerns.
liabilities: Direct N-halogen bonds occur in 207 of 870 optimizer observations, versus Parent 275. The seed-1 maximum carries N-Br and N-F, and its fused unsaturated four-membered ring adds a separate geometric concern; the seed-2 maximum also carries N-F.

Small perceived rings occur in 200 observations versus Parent 64; S-halogen bonds occur in 43 versus 3. The late sulfur-chloride examples show that conventional amide connectivity does not resolve peripheral local-bond concerns. These counts are structural observations, not stability or synthesis measurements.
missing_features: The tiny and doubled products fail to preserve the useful compact arrangement. The record does not identify an exact absent target pharmacophore.

The leading amide families do not consistently provide alternative local substitutions free of N-halogen bonds or small-ring geometric questions; the halogen-on-carbon seed-0 series is an explicit counterexample to a universal N-halogen requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied trimethoxyindole anilide initially scores 0.3051048083696145. Child seed maxima are 0.4349635367667153, 0.4478476056206344 and 0.4519753205796759; published Parent maxima are 0.4593573492521118, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.4369542269692598. The Parent seed-0 maximum is an N-hydroxy azaaryl amide without N-halogen bonding; seed 2 uses adjacent thiocarbonyl/carbonyl groups. Within Child seed 0, aryl Br and F examples tie at 0.4349635367667153. Within seed 2, adding the aryl fluorine to the cited 0.4339692349432291 example gives 0.4519753205796759, whereas adding another ring methyl gives 0.3116924902171652. Small N or interhalogen species score 0.0; a 47-heavy-atom doubled indole-anilide scores 1.5264774297846512e-15. The visible gradient favours a complete compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement, with local substitution sensitivity; aromatic mass, halogen presence or nitrogen count alone does not explain it.

per_task.generated_character: The output shifts toward large connected azaaromatic/dione assemblies: median heavy-atom count is 44.5 versus Parent 31, with seed medians 46, 52 and 40. The Child seed leaders have 61, 58 and 39 heavy atoms and respectively 5, 8 and 5 perceived rings. Seed 0 joins a fused dione to several nitrogen heterocycles, imine-containing chains and repeated N-formyl/urea-like carbonyl branches through an N-O-containing connection. Seed 1 has repeated nitrogen-rich diones, a methylthio pyridyl region, ester-linked polyenes, ring N-Cl and an oxygen-containing four-membered closure. Seed 2 is a dichloroaryl ester linked to an aza-fused dione and a carbamoyl amino-azaaryl region; the latter has two perceived four-membered cycles. Ester, amide and heteroaromatic groups are familiar individually, but the joined structures do not come with synthesis or geometry evidence. Parent seed leaders are smaller at 30, 36 and 28 heavy atoms.
liabilities: N-halogen graph incidence is 192 of 870 versus Parent 39; O-O incidence is 112 versus 80. Some large examples also carry imine chains, long polyenes or N-O connections. These are context-dependent structural concerns, not a claim that every N-N or N-O heterocycle is unacceptable.

Perceived four-membered closures occur in the seed-1 and seed-2 leaders. The much larger seed-0 and seed-1 leaders require complex connectivity without route evidence; neither size nor RDKit aromatic flags establish synthetic feasibility.
missing_features: The Child does not show the Parent seed-0 compact high-label connectivity among its leaders; it mainly supplies larger dione-linked alternatives. The observed comparison does not reveal a unique missing fragment that should be inserted.

Conventional, geometrically resolved alternatives to the unusual connected small-ring and N-halogen arrangements are not established at the leading Child labels. Rich ring inventory is already present.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child seed maxima are 0.5962169254318828, 0.5987567945751036 and 0.5994200497100248, versus published Parent 0.8561477222467935, 0.6204376881838878 and 0.6442339647723496. The Parent seed-0 molecule is a compact linked/fused aza-carbonyl/thione system bearing O-F and a halomethyl ether; its late evaluation-281 maximum is retained in this comparison despite its own chemistry concerns. Child tiny fragments such as C#N and ClBr sit at 0.5. The highest Child linked-heterocycle labels sit close together: replacing the seed-2 amino substituent with methoxy gives 0.5991465222057546 versus 0.5994200497100248, and altering a terminal polyene in seed 1 leaves the 0.5987567945751036 label unchanged. A 114-heavy-atom elaboration reaches only 0.5695950199342519. Thus linked heterocyclic/carbonyl context associates with improvement above the observed floor, while more size, more repeats or more unsaturation does not reproduce the Parent high-label molecular arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The high-label structures combine aromatic regions with aliphatic amines, rather than showing a shortage of amine centres. Optimizer heavy-atom median is 32 versus Parent 29. Seed leaders have 28, 29 and 31 heavy atoms, with two aromatic rings each. Seed 0 combines an N-propyl pyrrolidine, a substituted amino linker bearing N-S-H, a ring-closed aryl/carbocyclic region and an aminophenol. Seed 1 has a benzene-associated medium-ring tertiary amine, an aminoalkyl/enamine connection and a fluorophenol, plus carbon-bound Br/F. Seed 2 instead has a benzene-associated four-membered nitrogen ring, an N-butyl chain, terminal alkyne, fluorinated carbon, aminoethylamino substituent and an O-C=N group. These share broad aryl/amine organization but differ in ring topology and peripheral functionality. The Child contains more large outliers, up to 106 heavy atoms.
liabilities: The best seed-0 molecule carries an N-S-H connection, whereas other high-label molecules lack it. The seed-1 enamine and seed-2 O-C=N substituent and small nitrogen ring require environment-specific assessment; the record does not establish their stability or makeability.

RDKit perceives unassigned centres in 787 of 870 Child observations versus Parent 839, with no specified chiral atom tags. The neutral SMILES do not imply a lack of potentially protonatable amines. A 106-heavy-atom concatenation scores only 0.028858377891050647.
missing_features: The lower-scoring seed-2 series has amines and aromatic groups already, but does not reproduce the same complete high-label spatial/connectivity arrangements as the other seeds. No precise missing receptor contact can be inferred from these SMILES and scores.
The generated chiral carbon arrangements lack specified stereochemical identity; solution protonation and accessible conformations were not established for these amine-rich graphs.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child seed maxima are 0.9961652782614213, 0.9832537232778018 and 0.8315231336962678; Parent maxima are 0.9912539132815379, 0.9999994532254913 and 0.9817975835038065. The Parent seed-1 leader is a seven-membered cyclic diamine with aryl/arylalkyl groups and a methylthio substituent; it shows that a recognizable cyclic aryl-amine arrangement already attains a high supplied label. Child seed-2 early N-sulfonyl cyclic amide scores 0.0002562175393167918, and a quinoline bearing an O-NMe2 side chain scores 0.0002502134770627664. A direct aromatic sulfonyl bromide scores 0.0004426865581623269. Thus aromaticity, nitrogen presence or sulfur alone is insufficient; the richer aliphatic-amine/aryl arrangements associate with higher labels. The seed-2 late branched aminoethyl analogue scores 0.7616255141651985 versus its 0.8315231336962678 unbranched leader. These are structural score associations, not measurements of pKa, binding geometry, selectivity or receptor activity.

per_task.generated_character: These are mostly polycyclic aryl/azaaryl compounds connected to nitrogen/carbonyl ring systems, with median 30 heavy atoms versus Parent 31. Child seed leaders have 35, 35 and 32 heavy atoms. Seed 0 combines an ethoxypyridyl-substituted imide-like ring, a benzofused nitrogen ring and a methylene-substituted oxygen heterocycle; its five perceived rings include two aromatic rings. Seed 1 instead carries methoxyquinoline, a ring-closed aryl N-formyl/ether arrangement, an N-methyl saturated nitrogen ring and a small N-O/carbonyl ring. Its seven perceived basis cycles are not seven independent pharmacophores. Seed 2 links quinoline to ethoxy-substituted unsaturated nitrogen/urea-like carbonyl rings; the leader has two aromatic six-membered rings and two perceived eight-membered cycles. Carbonyl groups, azaarenes and amines are present, but larger ring systems, small N-O closures and fused arrangements have no demonstrated synthesis or conformer evidence.
liabilities: Perceived small rings occur in 250 of 870 Child observations versus Parent 114. Some leaders or late alternatives contain small N-O/carbonyl rings, N-N links or unsaturated medium rings; these call for individual assessment rather than a universal ban on such functional classes.

O-halogen bonds occur in 85 observations versus Parent 1, although the three Child seed leaders lack them. Unspecified tetrahedral centres occur in 495 observations versus Parent 645. Final proposals are chemically variable and are not necessarily the retained best molecules.
missing_features: Intact useful aryl/nitrogen/carbonyl relationships are missing from the tiny fragments, while elaboration does not supply a demonstrated higher-label alternative. The available gradient does not specify an exact missing target scaffold.
Geometric and stereochemical identity remains incomplete for the diverse ring-closed families; there is no evidence that adding more rings or heteroatoms would supply the residual missing chemistry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child seed maxima are 0.19802305885805252, 0.19045711137658072 and 0.2149896558044248, versus Parent 0.2144511711621884, 0.2214095461892601 and 0.23233384457488657. The Parent seed-2 leader already combines quinoline and a nitrogen/carbonyl bicyclic arrangement at 29 heavy atoms. The Child near-leader with an extra small carbonyl/oxygen ring and N-N/imine changes scores 0.2144511711621884, close to the seed-2 maximum despite multiple structural changes. Replacing the seed-2 leader ring NH by O gives 0.2117861279741904; this small observed difference is not a general heteroatom rule. C=N, FOSCl and NCO give 0.0. The 63-heavy-atom doubled nitrogen/carbonyl arrangement gives 0.16138097707050703. The visible association is retention of linked aryl/azaaryl and nitrogen/carbonyl context; increasing repetition or ring count does not systematically improve the supplied labels.

per_task.generated_character: Median size is 27 heavy atoms in both Child and Parent, and the Child seed leaders have 27, 28 and 27. Seed 0 gives a fluorinated enolic fused polycycle joined to a nitrogen-rich dione, with a cyclobutene substituent, a further four-membered closure and an N-N-F terminus. Its maximum itself has no cumulated carbon centre, but its broader series contains many small-ring cumulenes. Seed 1 joins an N-fluoro fused dione bearing a fluoroethyl substituent to an aryl-bridged aminoketone region with another fluoromethyl group. Seed 2 retains an aryl-linked N-fluoro dione with a nitrogen bearing hydroxyl and fluoromethoxy substituents. These are different fluorinated polar families, not one common fluorinated scaffold. The seed-1 and seed-2 leaders each have three aromatic rings; seed 0 has two. Conventional carbonyl and carbon-bound fluorine chemistry coexists with unusual N-halogen/N-O substitution and demanding connected-ring geometries.
liabilities: Direct N-halogen bonds occur in 513 of 870 Child observations versus Parent 425; all three Child seed leaders contain N-F. The seed-2 nitrogen bears two oxygen-linked substituents, a different local environment from an ordinary amine or ether.

Carbon-centred cumulated double bonds in perceived rings of size at most seven occur in 127 Child observations, all from seed 0, versus Parent 1. The cited cyclic cumulene at 0.492860958701208 is not the seed-0 maximum; losing the cumulene at the maximum does not remove its separate four-membered closures. These are graph-based geometric concerns, not measured conformational impossibility.

There are 117 observations with at most five heavy atoms versus Parent 33, and 529 with unassigned tetrahedral centres versus Parent 439. Tiny fragments continue late, including the seed-2 evaluation-295 ethene, so last proposal chemistry must not be confused with the best observed endpoint.
missing_features: The Child leading families do not consistently supply conventional local nitrogen substitution and independently established ring geometry alongside the favourable compact polar organization. The record cannot identify an exact missing pharmacophore or infer that simply adding fluorine helps.

Specified stereochemical identity is absent where substituted ring carbons can be stereogenic. Enol/imine and N-O-containing structures also have unresolved chemical-state questions; neither stereochemical nor tautomeric benefits were measured.

Many tiny fragments have floor labels; large repeated assemblies also fail to match compact leaders, including the recorded 47-, 53- and 63-heavy-atom examples. transferable_gaps.gap: The generator inconsistently preserves useful multigroup molecular context when simplifying or elaborating a structure.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make task-local feedback available to transformations that preserve useful relationships between aromatic, carbonyl and amine regions while allowing genuine simplification and useful growth. This conditional output association supports testing context preservation, not imposing a fixed size floor or ceiling, prescribing a benchmark scaffold, or attributing fragmentation to a particular component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In n-37a4fc183d94 versus n-1744a1494180 under the complete current-profile Search panel, direct graph incidences are N-halogen 1033 versus 786, O-halogen 170 versus 217, S-halogen 76 versus 93 and O-O 166 versus 128, out of 4350 optimizer observations per node. Leading examples include N-F, N-Br, N-Cl, N-N-F, N-S-H and multiply oxygen-substituted nitrogen; other high-label examples lack these motifs. These mixed changes re-observe the local-environment gap recorded in n-1744a1494180 and traced there to n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a. The retained sulfur source condition was narrow; no new sulfur-admission audit or broader chemical-quality guarantee is inferred here.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently separate conventional local functional-group environments from unusual heteroatom attachments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer conventional alternative substitutions that retain useful group arrangements learned from the current session, and distinguish whole functional environments rather than element presence alone. Preserve useful amides, heterocycles, N-O motifs and sulfur chemistry where appropriate. A motif flag is a reason for context-sensitive assessment, not proof of instability, toxicity or a guaranteed score benefit from filtering.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This is the ring-geometry gap recorded in n-1744a1494180 with provenance from n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a, re-observed in n-37a4fc183d94 under the complete current-profile Search panel. RDKit parses all 4350 optimizer records, yet 129 contain a carbon centre with two double bonds in a perceived ring of size at most seven, versus Parent 6. Of those Child cases, 127 are concentrated in one seed of one fluorinated family, so the pooled count does not establish a uniform shift. Other leaders have unsaturated four-membered rings, small N-O/carbonyl rings or dense bridge closures. Conventional ring systems also occur; ring richness itself is not missing.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks demonstrated control of chemically credible geometry when changing ring connections and unsaturation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Distinguish ring size, bridge connectivity and bond geometry during ring-changing transformations, while offering alternatives that preserve learned functional relationships. Do not equate aromatic flags or descriptor-cell membership with accessible conformations. These observations do not justify a blanket ban on small or medium rings, identify a causal component, or establish that a geometry constraint improves scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The stereochemical-identity gap recorded by n-1744a1494180, originating in n-c55c3d520a2c and carried through n-62daf219c70a, persists in n-37a4fc183d94 on the complete current-profile Search panel. Every digest stereocentre-text incidence is zero. Independent RDKit perception finds unspecified tetrahedral centres in 2034 of 4350 Child optimizer observations versus Parent 2455; neither output has specified chiral atom tags. Some leading graphs have no perceived tetrahedral centre, and the smaller pooled count also coexists with many more tiny fragments. It is not evidence of improved identity control.
transferable_gaps.gap: Potentially stereogenic generated structures remain incompletely specified as chemical identities.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or resolve stereochemical information where molecular identity requires it, while treating achiral and configurationally unstable cases separately. Protonation, tautomerism and accessible conformations require separate assessment. The observed labels do not establish a stereochemical penalty, and this gap does not prescribe any objective-specific stereoisomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-37a4fc183d94 versus n-1744a1494180, under the same complete current-profile Search panel. The Child has 1717 distinct typed Murcko cores versus Parent 1740, and 1161 generic frameworks versus 1016, including the empty scaffold. Nonetheless, within two separate seeds of one compact aromatic family, each seed's 20 highest-label observations all share one typed core. Other seeds show multiple leading cores and different families, so this is local concentration rather than global scaffold collapse. This retains the conditional alternatives gap recorded by n-1744a1494180 with provenance from n-c55c3d520a2c through n-62daf219c70a.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically independent conventional alternatives to leading local families are not consistently demonstrated.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer independent connectivities that retain favourable relationships inferred from accepted local observations, and assess their actual labels and chemical quality separately. Neither additional descriptor niches, more generic frameworks nor distinct SMILES establishes useful chemical alternatives. This output association provides no component attribution or evidence that increasing diversity alone helps.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
